summary: The patch replaces the backtracking regex in trimLiterals with a linear indexOf-based walk. In 1,000,000 random inputs over quotes, spaces, tabs, newlines and double quotes, its output matched the old regex exactly, including the old regex's handling of unterminated and odd-quote tails. It handles 15M-character literals in about 50 ms, the worst-case inputs I tried ran in linear time, and the new tests cover each acceptance point.

findings.claim: The rule for recovering an unterminated literal at its last '' pair is subtle and has only one targeted test. It is correct: random-input comparison with the old regex found no difference. But a future change to this branch could drift from the regex's behaviour without being noticed. A table-driven test comparing against the old regex on small inputs would protect it.
findings.repro: node /tmp/fuzz.mjs  (compares trimLiterals with the old regex on 500k random strings; 0 mismatches)
